problem_summary.summary: In a sorted array of distinct integers, return the target's index or the index where it belongs to preserve sorted order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a sorted integer array nums and an integer target. Return the matching index, or the insertion index if absent.

brute_force.explanation: Scan from left to right and return the first index whose value is at least target. If no such value exists, the insertion point is the array length.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Because nums is sorted, the first value at least target is exactly the first position where target can be inserted without changing order. If there is no such value, target belongs after every element.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n), where n is nums.length; in the worst case every element is inspected.

optimized.explanation: Use a half-open binary-search interval [left, right) to find the lower bound: the first index whose value is at least target. When nums[mid] is too small, discard mid and everything before it; otherwise keep mid as a possible answer.
optimized.correctness_idea: The interval always contains the first qualifying index, or is empty when that index is nums.length. Each comparison removes half the candidates while preserving the lower-bound position, so left is the insertion index when the interval closes.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log n), where n is nums.length.

steps.condition: 5 < 6, so indices 0 and 1 cannot be the insertion point.
7 >= 6, so index 2 remains a possible lower bound.

steps.action: Return left, the first index at which target can be inserted.

edge_cases.case: Target is smaller than every value
Target is larger than every value

edge_cases.handling: The lower bound is its existing index.
The search returns either 0 or 1 according to the target's position.
